newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index dragged down by Siemens fall.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index dragged down by Siemens fall.

text.p: The German DAX index started floor dealings on Thursday lower, dragged down by a sharp fall in the shares of German electronic firm Siemens, which had already tumbled in Wednesday's post-bourse electronic trade.
Siemens, the fifth-heaviest stock among the 30 leading shares which make up the DAX index, had forecast a flat output for the 1996/97 financial year on Wednesday after the close of floor dealings.
The stock fell almost nine percent, dropping to a new year low of 72.90 marks, then recovered slightly to stand down 6.80 marks at 73.40 marks.
The DAX index, which had hovered around its closing level before Siemens traded on the floor, was down 12.20 points, or 0.45 percent, at 2,716.99 points.
Dealers said lower German government bonds and a weaker dollar, bad for German exporters, were also weighing on the market, overshadowing an overnight record close on Wall Street.

But they said they expected the German share market to consolidate for the rest of the day. "I expect we'll go sideways or slightly lower. A bit of a rest would be completely healthy," said one trader.
Meanwhile Daimler slipped slightly, losing nine pfennigs to 92.60 marks, after releasing nine month sales which were mainly in line with expectations.
The industrial giant reported first nine month sales of 75.9 billion marks, up from 72.8 billion a year earlier, a figure one dealer said was "not bad."
But dealers said a dip in sales at Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA) to 8.28 billion marks from 8.91 billion marks a year ago was somewhat disappointing.
They added that Daimler, in line with the rest of the German car sector, was suffering from the weaker dollar.

The chemical sector, on the other hand, was stronger than the market trend, led by Hoechst, up 1.10 marks at 61.20 marks, continuing to climb after its nine month results released on Wednesday were well-received.
The stock had earlier touched a record high of 61.30 marks.
